questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Historical Time Spans' refers to.
questions.a: History involves analyzing transformations that happen over a duration rather than just identifying specific calendar days.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Historical Time Spans'.
questions.a: Historical processes often occur over long periods rather than on a single date.

questions.a: The significance of specific dates is determined by the particular events or themes a historian chooses to emphasize.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Selection of Historical Dates'.
questions.a: Dates are not important on their own but become vital based on the focus of the study.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'James Mill's Periodisation' refers to.
questions.a: A 19th-century classification that split Indian history into three stages based on the primary religion of the rulers.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'James Mill's Periodisation'.
questions.a: Dividing history based on the religion of the ruling elite.

questions.a: A Western-influenced division of history into ancient, medieval, and modern periods, where 'modern' signifies progress and reason.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Modern Periodisation and its Critique'.
questions.a: Applying Western concepts of modernity to Indian history.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Concept of Colonisation' refers to.
questions.a: The political, social, and economic dominance of one country over another that results in fundamental structural changes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Concept of Colonisation'.

questions.a: The British practice of documenting every policy and decision to facilitate study, debate, and governance.
